note.en: Rack-scale product with very limited on-demand access: CoreWeave still lists the cheapest published rate (~$10.50/GPU-hr), while GetDeploying's 9-provider tracker average edged up to ~$18.79/GPU-hr as more enterprise-only listings entered pricing indexes; hyperscaler bare-metal (Azure ND GB200 v6) tops out at ~$27/GPU-hr. Most capacity (Together AI, Oracle, Azure) is still sold as reserved contracts with quote-only pricing; CoreWeave will quote 1-year terms on request (~35% off list) but publishes no rate card.

Floor shifted providers: Vultr repriced its early-access B200 up to ~$8.50/GPU-hr, so Verda is now the cheapest on-demand listing at ~$3.12/GPU-hr. Typical on-demand eased to ~$6.99/GPU-hr (-9% vs the prior check) as new Blackwell capacity from Nebius, Lambda and CoreWeave started catching up with demand, while Google Cloud's a4-highgpu-8g stays the ceiling at $16.11/GPU-hr. No clean published 1-year rate.

Newest AMD flagship with a thin rental market: Vultr's 8x pods remain the floor at ~$2.59/GPU-hr, but the typical price has drifted up sharply to ~$7.15/GPU-hr as OVHcloud (~$7.10) and CoreWeave (~$7.20) on-demand became the more representative listings, with Oracle bare metal still topping the range at $8.60/GPU-hr. CoreWeave's 1-year reservation holds at $4.25/GPU-hr — a ~41% discount to its own on-demand rate. Coverage is still thin (3-4 tracked providers), so treat the median move as directional.

Min from FluidStack ($2.30, unchanged); typical neocloud range drifted up slightly to ~$4.3/GPU-hr (AIMultiple ~$4.11, GetDeploying's cross-provider median ~$4.48) as booked-out capacity through Aug-Sep 2026 pushes demand pressure. Hyperscaler ceiling holds at Azure's ND96isr H200 v5, ~$13.78/GPU-hr — no reserved SKU exists for that instance. Reserved-rate listings still average ~$3.72/GPU-hr.

Widest rental market (48+ providers): marketplace/neocloud low end still $1.49/GPU-hr (Vast.ai), typical price eased to ~$3.30/GPU-hr (AIMultiple reads closer to $3.15) as more budget-tier PCIe capacity (Thunder Compute ~$2.19) entered the pool. The hyperscaler ceiling holds near Azure's ND96isr H100 v5 at ~$11.06/GPU-hr. Per SemiAnalysis, 1-year contract rates were around $2.35/GPU-hr as of spring 2026; the firm's own shortage commentary points to continued month-on-month increases on the reserved side, though no fresher published number has surfaced.

sources.label: Vantage — Azure ND96isr H100 v5 instance pricing

note.en: Aggressively priced for its 192GB of HBM3: TensorWave anchors the low end at ~$1.71/GPU-hr, while Azure/Oracle's 8x on-demand list price tops the range at $6.00/GPU-hr. Typical pricing cooled to ~$3.20/GPU-hr as mid-tier providers (Crusoe, Hot Aisle) came in below the prior median. DigitalOcean now publishes a clean 12-month reserved rate of $1.91/GPU-hr (26% off its $2.59 on-demand rate), effective Aug 2026.

Legacy workhorse in steady decline: Thunder Compute now undercuts the field at ~$1.09/GPU-hr, RunPod/Lambda cluster at $1.39-2.79, with GCP a2-ultragpu still listing ~$5.07/GPU-hr at the top. GetDeploying's tracked median has ticked up only slightly to ~$1.76-1.80/GPU-hr. Civo now publishes a clean tiered 80GB rate card — $1.79 on-demand, $1.59 at 12 months, down to $1.39 at 36 months — the first widely visible 1-year reference rate for this GPU; most other contract demand has moved to H100/H200.

sources.label: Civo — NVIDIA A100 GPU cloud pricing

note.en: Floor dropped further: Lium.io now lists the cheapest tracked rate at ~$0.38/GPU-hr (Des Moines), below TensorDock's prior $0.47 anchor. Typical pricing eased to ~$0.90/GPU-hr as budget-tier neocloud listings (Omega Gradient, GPU Outlet, Packet AI, all $0.47-0.54) cluster below the old median, and the hyperscaler ceiling holds at Oracle Cloud's ~$3.50/GPU-hr. Civo now publishes a tiered rate card — $1.29 on-demand down to $1.09 at 12 months and $0.89 at 36 months.

sources.label: Civo — NVIDIA L40S GPU cloud pricing

note.en: Consumer flagship on marketplaces only (no hyperscaler offering): Salad Cloud still floors the market at ~$0.25/GPU-hr, RunPod Secure Cloud unchanged at $0.99 the published top. Typical pricing has actually ticked up to ~$0.55-0.66/GPU-hr (ComputePrices, AIMultiple) as more mainstream providers (RunPod, Sesterce, GPU Outlet) list capacity at $0.68-0.84 rather than at marketplace-floor rates — reversing the prior drift toward RTX 4090 levels even as the low end holds flat.

Vast.ai's marketplace floor holds at ~$0.13/GPU-hr, while serverless-billed providers keep the ceiling near $1.61/GPU-hr (GetDeploying/AIMultiple aggregate) as Beam-style endpoint configs list up to $1.77/GPU-hr. Typical pricing has eased to ~$0.44/GPU-hr, down from ~$0.60/GPU-hr a year ago — RunPod Secure Cloud's $0.69 remains well off the tracked reference points on either side.
